name: Baxter International
description: Baxter makes the supplies and equipment around an IV drip and a hospital bed: IV solutions, infusion pumps and sets, surgical sealants, hospital beds, patient monitoring and connected-care software (from the Hillrom acquisition), plus injectable drugs, inhaled anesthetics and drug compounding. Pumps and beds are capital, while IV solutions, sets and drugs recur with patient volume. 2025 was a hard year: an operating loss of $308M after $485M of goodwill and $290M of other asset impairments, Hurricane Helene costs at its North Carolina IV plant and Class I recalls of its Novum pump; the quarterly dividend was cut to $0.01. It sold Kidney Care (now Vantive) to Carlyle on 2025-01-31 for $3.8 billion.

sub.name: Surgical and hospital devices and diagnostics

employees.note: after the Kidney Care sale; 15,100 US and 22,400 outside the US

businessLines.name: Medical Products & Therapies
businessLines.how: Sells IV solutions, infusion pumps and administration sets, and surgical sealants and hemostats to hospitals; pumps are placed as capital and the sets and fluids are re-bought continuously.

businessLines.name: Healthcare Systems & Technologies
businessLines.how: Sells hospital beds and surfaces, patient monitoring, connected-care software and front-line diagnostic devices to hospitals and clinics; capital equipment plus service and software contracts.

businessLines.name: Pharmaceuticals
businessLines.how: Sells specialty injectable drugs and inhaled anesthetics to hospitals, and compounds IV drugs (mostly outside the US), on repeat orders.

businessLines.name: Other (not in a segment)
businessLines.how: Mainly product sales to Vantive under a Kidney Care manufacturing and supply agreement, plus products and services from certain plants.

brands.name: Hillrom (acquired December 2021)
brands.note: source of the Healthcare Systems & Technologies segment ($3,071M in 2025)
